question: Which mountain range forms the eastern boundary of the Deccan Plateau?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Eastern Ghats**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Eastern Ghats** form the **eastern boundary of the Deccan Plateau**, running parallel to the eastern coastal plains of India.
 
• The mountain range stretches from the state of **Odisha** in the north to **Tamil Nadu** in the south, passing through Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The **highest peak** in the Eastern Ghats is **Arma Konda**, located in Andhra Pradesh, with an elevation of 1,680 meters (5,512 ft).
 
• Unlike the Western Ghats, the Eastern Ghats are **discontinuous and fragmented**, primarily due to rivers like the Godavari, Mahanadi, and Krishna cutting across the range.
 
• The Eastern Ghats are known for their unique **biodiversity** and are home to several wildlife sanctuaries, including the **Simlipal National Park** in Odisha and **Seshachalam Hills** in Andhra Pradesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Satpura Range:**

 
 
• The Satpura Range is a series of hills in central India that runs parallel to the Vindhya Range.
 
• It is located to the north of the Deccan Plateau, separating it from the Indo-Gangetic Plain.
 
• The highest peak of the Satpura Range is **Dhupgarh**, with an elevation of 1,350 meters (4,429 ft).
 
 
 
• **Vindhya Range:**
 
 
• The Vindhya Range runs across central India, separating the Indo-Gangetic Plains from the Deccan Plateau.
 
• The range is historically significant as it has acted as a cultural and geographical boundary between North and South India.
 
• The highest point of the Vindhya Range is **Sad-Bhawna Shikhar**, with an elevation of around 752 meters (2,467 ft).
 
 
 
• **Western Ghats:**
 
 
• The Western Ghats, also known as the Sahyadri Hills, form the western boundary of the Deccan Plateau.
 
• This range stretches parallel to the western coast of India, covering states like Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, and Kerala.
 
• The highest peak in the Western Ghats is **Anamudi**, located in Kerala, with an elevation of 2,695 meters (8,842 ft).
 
 
 
• **Eastern Ghats:**
 
 
• The Eastern Ghats are older than the Western Ghats and are composed primarily of ancient rocks like charnockites and granites.
 
• Key rivers like the **Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri**, and **Mahanadi** pass through these ranges, forming fertile deltas at their mouths.
 
• The Eastern Ghats are home to several tribes and support a variety of flora and fauna, including endangered species like the **Indian Pangolin**.
